dlg.holloway.first.0.note: Hard and clipped. Threat flat, not shouted. Name and rank at the end tired and bitter: 'what's left of'.

dlg.holloway.first.1.note: Grudging. 'I'd thank you, but...' dry and tired. Name and rank flat.

dlg.holloway.first.2.note: 'At night.' its own suspicious beat. Clipped and hoarse.

dlg.holloway.hub.0.note: An effort to say. 'Don't tell anyone I said so.' gruff, nearly a smile.

dlg.holloway.hub.1.intent: a man of his was killed
dlg.holloway.hub.1.note: Quartermaster's list for a dead man. 'by the bad leg' barely steady. No crack: 'I'd give a month's pay to hear him hum.' is the grief itself (paying is the nearest he gets to sorry), flatter and slower than the rest. Then straight back to business: 'Five a pelt, still. What do you want?'

dlg.holloway.hub.2.note: Narrator reads the business with the letter. 'What.' flat and closed.

dlg.holloway.hub.6.note: Not proud. The Maeca line hurts more than he lets on.

dlg.holloway.hub.7.note: Exasperated. 'and I hate that' with feeling.

dlg.holloway.wolves.0.note: A quartermaster's numbers. 'Bring me proof and I'll pay. Bring me stories and I won't.' as a rule. The eleven-men line bitter and dry.

dlg.holloway.maeca.0.note: Fair-minded first sentence. Then much quieter, after a pause: what she never got. Guilt he won't name.

dlg.holloway.ashford.0.note: 'Boots, for a start.' heavy. Bitter pride on 'I was good at it.' Then the door slams: 'That's all you're getting.' 'Something else?' brusque.

dlg.holloway.bounty.0.note: Almost respectful of the old devil. Thanks offered plainly.

dlg.holloway.liar.0.wants: his gold's worth, and the truth
dlg.holloway.liar.0.hides: he has been paying for something himself for ten years; some of the anger is at himself for trusting you
dlg.holloway.liar.0.note: Quiet anger one notch below the surface; he never raises his voice and swears rarely, so when he does it lands. Mock-quote 'dealt with'. 'So.' then the swear lands hard and low, not shouted.

dlg.holloway.repaid.0.note: Dry wit; 'I've written both halves down' a quartermaster's threat.

dlg.holloway.argued.0.note: Turning it over. 'bucket against a flood' tired. Deal offered gruffly.

dlg.holloway.defied.0.note: His anger stays one notch below the surface; he doesn't shout at a person. 'Out of my sight.' sharp but level. The threat about the cell-rats almost pleasant.

dlg.holloway.caravan2.0.note: Quiet. 'I don't like a single name on it.' troubled.

dlg.holloway.sick.0.note: Dismissive first line; after the pause, open and tired: he'd rather fix the cause.

dlg.holloway.cause.0.note: 'Of course it's the lamplings.' disgust. Firm: no paying men to kill sick dogs.

dlg.holloway.cause.1.note: 'Of course it's the lamplings.' disgust. Practical deal.

dlg.holloway.lie.0.note: Not convinced. The last sentence a warning.

dlg.holloway.expose.0.note: Reading the ledger aloud, building. Contempt and relish on 'you careful, greedy little man'. The fee line dry: 'Once.'

dlg.holloway.expose.1.note: Reading the ledger, building. Contempt on 'careful, greedy little man'. Then awkward, sincere thanks; 'I've not much to pay you with' rueful.

dlg.holloway.cb_killed_greymuzzle.1.note: Dry joke about Maeca. After the pause, unexpectedly reflective: odd, missing a thing you hated.

dlg.holloway.cb_burned_roost.0.note: Each clause measured and cold. 'and I'd like you to know that I know that' quiet and precise.

dlg.holloway.cb_freed_teamsters.0.note: Relief in 'and alive'. The joke at his own expense dry.

dlg.holloway.cb_tricked_redcowl.0.note: Deadpan 'The Watch was in bed.' The last three sentences a man talking himself round.

dlg.holloway.cb_opened_vault.0.note: Solemn, then too tired to care. 'What's down there?' genuinely wanting to know.

dlg.holloway.say_calling.0.note: Interested for a moment; 'I can't afford you either way' rueful.

dlg.holloway.say_woman.0.note: Starts the old line, stops himself. 'it's no place.' flat and honest.

dlg.holloway.t_holloway.0.note: A list delivered like an inventory, tired and longing. 'In that order.' dry. The dog line sheepish.

dlg.holloway.ledger_early.0.wants: not to be made to act yet
dlg.holloway.ledger_early.0.note: Narrator for the reading. Then reading the entries, quieter as he understands. Firm and low on 'Don't tell me where you got it.'

dlg.holloway.ledger_early2.0.note: Dry about thieves and letters. Proof, not evidence. 'Keep it somewhere I can't see it.' low.

dlg.holloway.post.0.note: Narrator holds the silence. Then quiet questions he knows the answers to. 'Corran.' on its own. The deserter lines in self-disgust.

dlg.holloway.post2.0.note: Thinking it through. Narrator for the writing. 'So somebody had oil. And a reason.' cold. The apology line heavy.

dlg.holloway.letter.0.note: 'Mine.' hard. Narrator: the cup doesn't move. 'Read your own post, if anybody writes to you.' is curt cover; he looks at you a beat too long before it.
dlg.holloway.letter.0.hides: the letter is about you: the north asks for "the one from the ford"
